claims.claim: Energy Fuels links domestic mineral feedstocks and White Mesa processing to uranium and rare-earth separation, serving nuclear-fuel and magnet-material supply chains; heavy-REE construction directly targets a processing bottleneck between mineral resource and qualified separated material.

The successor bottleneck is commercial-scale qualification and economics: construction progress does not yet prove yields, operating costs, feedstock continuity or customer acceptance for Tb/Dy output.

risks.risk: Feedstock, commissioning, qualification and commodity-price conditions can shift the bottleneck downstream even after plant construction completes.

contradictions.contradiction: Technical and construction milestones improve execution evidence, but commercial-scale heavy-REE economics remain prospective.

unknowns.unknown: Commercial Tb/Dy yields, costs and customer qualification remain unproven.

claims.claim: Construction of commercial heavy-REE capacity is meaningful execution evidence but does not yet validate commercial economics; conditional government financing likewise should not be treated as closed funding.
The multi-commodity model can diversify opportunity but also exposes execution to uranium and rare-earth price cycles, feedstock availability and simultaneous project demands.

risks.risk: Commercial heavy-REE scale-up may underperform on yield, cost, ramp or qualification despite successful construction.
Financing and commodity exposure can increase dilution or capital-allocation pressure if project cash generation lags.

contradictions.contradiction: Technical and construction milestones materially improve execution evidence, but commercial-scale heavy-REE economics remain prospective.

unknowns.unknown: Final financing mix and commercial heavy-REE economics remain unknown.
